Worrell, E. and Price, L. (2001). Policy scenarios for energy efficiency improvement in industry. Energy Policy 29, 1223-1241. PII S0301-4215(01)00069-6.

NO TECHNOLOGY PARAMETERS EXTRACTED. A policy-scenario paper (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, from the Clean Energy Future study run with CEF-NEMS): Tables 1-2 list policies and barriers; Table 3 primary energy use and Table 4 carbon emissions by sector and fuel (1990, 1997, 2010, 2020; BAU, Moderate, Advanced); Table 5 sector energy intensities (MJ/$ and primary-energy GJ/t for pulp and paper, glass, cement, iron and steel, aluminium; e.g. cement 5.5 GJ/t in 1997 falling to 3.7 GJ/t in 2020 Advanced); Table 6 annual total energy-service costs ($ billion/yr). Everything is sector aggregate and primary energy; no equipment-level SEC, cost, efficiency or emissions. The paper states 8.8 GW of new industrial CHP in the BAU scenario to 2020 (CHP excluded from the tables). The underlying technology analysis is in Interlaboratory Working Group (1997, 2000) and Worrell et al. 1999; use those instead.
